subject: Designated for assignment (DFA)
query: what does designated for assignment mean
title: What does designated for assignment mean? DFA in baseball
answer: Designated for assignment, or DFA, means an MLB team has removed a player from its 40-man roster. The club then has up to seven days to trade him, put him on waivers, or release him. Waivers take 48 hours, so in practice a team has about five days to find a trade.
body:
If another team claims the player on waivers, it takes over his contract. If no one claims him, his team can send him outright to the minors, though veterans with enough service time can refuse and become free agents. The player keeps being paid while he waits; that waiting period is often called "DFA limbo." The days between Christmas and New Year's Day do not count toward the seven.

DFAs come in waves in November. Teams must add prospects to the 40-man roster by Nov. 17, 2026 to protect them from the Rule 5 draft, and the non-tender deadline follows on Nov. 20, so clubs clear spots by designating fringe players. A player picked up in the Rule 5 draft cannot be designated from the draft until 20 days before Opening Day, and a player just claimed off waivers cannot be designated again for at least 48 hours.
in_the_news: MLB teams clear 40-man roster spots ahead of the Nov. 17, 2026 Rule 5 protection deadline, and DFA moves pile up each November.

faq.q: What does DFA mean in baseball?
faq.a: Designated for assignment: the team takes the player off its 40-man roster and has up to seven days to trade, waive or release him.

faq.q: Does a DFA player still get paid?
faq.a: Yes. He keeps his salary during the designation, and if released, the team still owes his guaranteed contract.

faq.q: Can a player refuse an outright assignment?
faq.a: Veterans with enough service time, or players previously outrighted, can reject a trip to the minors and become free agents.
